key_insight: Truncating positional encodings changes their theoretical power, making some popular spectral and walk-based graph features no longer equivalent.
engineering_relevance: For practical GNN design, this means truncated positional encodings should be chosen and combined carefully, since no single truncated family is universally strongest.
method: Analyzed expressive power of truncated spectral and walk-based positional encodings.
Compared closely related variants such as k-harmonic distances to expose differences under truncation.
Tested mixed truncated PE designs against single-family baselines on real-world datasets.
evidence_signal: The paper combines theoretical analysis with experiments on real-world datasets and reports that mixing truncated positional encodings performs better than using any one family alone.
watch_item: The conclusions apply to truncated, not complete, positional encodings, so implementation choices like k selection can materially change model expressivity.
paper_title: Understanding Truncated Positional Encodings for Graph Neural Networks
